---

Use a list of county FIPS codes to summarise the **ASTER Global Emissivity Dataset
(AG100 v003, 100 m)**. traktr loads the county boundaries, fetches the tiles they
intersect and exports area-weighted statistics with a data dictionary and
provenance report.

## Earthdata Login

AG100 is distributed by NASA LP DAAC. Store an Earthdata Login user token as
`EARTHDATA_TOKEN` in `~/.Renviron` and restart R, or configure an Earthdata Login
entry for `urs.earthdata.nasa.gov` in `~/.netrc`. The offline check reports the
detected method without printing credentials.
[Earthdata Login](https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov/)

```{r auth, eval = FALSE}
library(traktr)
earthdata_auth_check()
```

## Read the FIPS list

The input CSV has a header and a column of county FIPS codes. Change `col` if
the column is named differently. `read_fips_csv()` pads the codes to five digits
and warns when it removes missing or duplicate entries.

```{r fips, eval = FALSE}
fips <- read_fips_csv("fips.csv", col = "x")
```

## Load county boundaries

`aoi_us_counties()` loads the US Census cartographic boundary file at the selected
vintage and scale. Each row is a county or county equivalent keyed by `GEOID`.
The county polygons are stored as an area-of-interest attribute. The function
reports requested codes absent from the boundary file.

```{r counties, eval = FALSE}
cty <- aoi_us_counties(fips = fips, year = 2020, resolution = "500k")
names(cty)
#> GEOID STATEFP COUNTYFP NAME NAMELSAD STUSPS ALAND AWATER region
```

## Fetch ASTER tiles

`fetch_aster_ged()` requests only the 1° tiles that intersect the county polygons.
It converts each HDF5 granule to a GeoTIFF containing `elev`, `ndvi_mean`,
`ndvi_sd`, `temp_mean`, `temp_sd`, `lwm` and `nobs`. Rerun with the same output
directory to reuse existing GeoTIFFs.

```{r fetch, eval = FALSE}
cty <- fetch_aster_ged(cty, out_dir = "data/ag100")
attr(cty, "aster_ged_tiles")[, c("tile_id", "status", "size_bytes")]
```

## Summarise per county

```{r attach, eval = FALSE}
cty <- attach_aster_ged(cty, naming = "county")
cty[, c("GEOID", "NAME",
        "ASTER_county_elevation_mean", "ASTER_county_elevation_sd",
        "ASTER_ndvi_mean_mean", "ASTER_temp_mean_mean",
        "ASTER_lwm_water_perc", "county_area_km2_geodesic")]
```

Values default to the raw AG100 units, including NDVI × 100 and temperature in
centikelvin. With `convert = TRUE`, NDVI is divided by 100 and mean temperatures
are converted to degrees Celsius. Temperature standard deviations are converted
to kelvin.

### What the statistics mean

Each intersecting 100 m cell in the county contributes according to its area
inside the polygon. Standard deviations use the area-weighted population formula.
`missing_perc` is the percentage of mapped county area without a valid value,
including area in tiles without an AG100 granule. It is 100 when all mapped area
is missing and `NA` when no area was measured.

- Elevation `cin` is the percentage of valid area at exactly zero metres.
  Land/water `cin` is the percentage of mapped county area with a valid value.
- The observation flag `lt_4` indicates an area-weighted mean below four.
- Elevation `sum` is `NA` in polygon mode.

ecolo-zip samples points in a spiderweb pattern. County summaries use raster
cells across the whole polygon. As county area increases, elevation SD and the
range from minimum to maximum tend to grow. Use `county_area_km2_geodesic` as a
covariate. Set `naming = "ecolozip"` to use the column names expected by older
scripts.

### Known data gaps

In the 2022 county run, the elevation band was entirely missing in the
converted AG100 v003 tiles for Hawaii, so elevation statistics could not be
calculated for Hawaii counties. The cause has not been verified against the
original HDF5 files. ASTER GDEM artefacts such as isolated pits near water bodies can distort
elevation extrema. Minima reached about −280 m in the 2022 county run, so prefer
the mean or median. Some tiles in the Aleutians and on Bering Sea islands lack
AG100 granules. The affected county area counts toward `missing_perc`.

### Parallel processing and resuming

For larger runs, set a parallel `future::plan()` and pass `workers` to
`attach_aster_ged()`. The package leaves the future plan to the caller.
By default, extraction caches per-tile moments in `_moments/` inside the tile
directory. Rerunning the same extraction computes only the missing moments.

```{r parallel, eval = FALSE}
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)
cty <- attach_aster_ged(cty, workers = 4)
```

## Save the result

```{r write, eval = FALSE}
write_county_summary(cty, path = "output/us_counties_aster_2020")
```

This creates `us_counties_aster_2020.csv`,
`us_counties_aster_2020_dictionary.csv` and
`us_counties_aster_2020_PROVENANCE.md`. The CSV quotes `GEOID` as a string.
Import it as character to retain leading zeros. The dictionary records column
definitions, units and ecolo-zip names. The provenance report records the
boundary vintage, retrieval time and tile checksums. Add `"parquet"` to
`formats` to also export Parquet when `nanoparquet` is installed.
